issues.legal_issue: A village specified in the statutory schedule and held under a conditional agreement with the State constitutes an estate, even where the grant transfers ownership rather than a lease or farm.
material_facts: The villages were specified in the statutory schedule.

The grant transferred ownership of the villages and exempted the grantee from land revenue, subject to conditions including payment of annual rent if demanded and obligations concerning occupants and customary rights.
The grant did not merely transfer a right to enjoy the land for a term or in perpetuity, and the grantee was not required to account for or pay revenue as a farmer.
issues.conclusion: The villages constituted an estate because they were specified in the schedule and held under an agreement with the State; the grant was neither a lease nor a farm.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(b) and 2(d) of the Salsette Estates (Land Revenue Exemption Abolition) Act, 1951, an estate is a scheduled village or part of a village held under a lease, farm, or agreement with the State Government. A transfer of ownership subject to conditions governing the exemption from land revenue can constitute such an agreement, even though the transfer is not a lease or farm. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.village_is_scheduled: The village was included in the statutory schedule of villages covered by the enactment.
predicates.state_grant_subjects_revenue_exemption_t: The State transferred the village and made the grantee's exemption from land revenue subject to agreed conditions.

issues.definition: A scheduled village transferred by the State subject to conditions on its revenue exemption qualifies as an estate.

issues.legal_issue: An estate-holder cannot rely on the statutory saving for other persons to preserve the estate-holder's own exemption from land revenue.
material_facts: The estate-holder claimed that the grant exempting the estate from land revenue continued to protect the estate-holder after the enactment.
The exemption had been granted to the estate-holder under the arrangement governing the estate.
The statutory saving applied to a person other than the estate-holder who held land in the estate under a qualifying contract, grant, or law.
issues.conclusion: The estate-holder's exemption was not saved; the statutory saving protects qualifying rights of persons other than the estate-holder.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(1) and 3(3) of the Salsette Estates (Land Revenue Exemption Abolition) Act, 1951 impose land revenue liability on lands in an estate notwithstanding prior instruments, subject to the saving for a person other than the estate-holder who holds land exempt from land revenue under a special contract or grant made or recognized by the estate's governing arrangement, or under a law in force. The express exclusion of the estate-holder means that the estate-holder's own exemption is extinguished. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.land_is_in_an_estate: The land for which exemption is claimed forms part of an estate covered by the enactment.
predicates.claimant_is_estate_holder: The person claiming the exemption holds the estate.
predicates.exemption_was_granted_to_claimant: The claimed exemption from land revenue was granted to the person claiming it.

issues.definition: When an estate-holder claims an exemption granted to that holder for land in the estate, the exemption is not preserved.
